scenario.description: A festival exhibition producer must approve the operating package for an immersive film-and-sound installation in a heritage gallery, including the projection setup, audio asset, visitor route, timed-entry limits, and required production records.

shared_context.S1: The festival is installing an immersive film-and-sound work called 'Afterimage Corridor' in the east gallery of the Marlowe Heritage Centre.
shared_context.S2: The current installation draft calls for four LED projection units, a continuous audio loop, entry through the north doorway, and open walk-in admission.
shared_context.S3: Mara has final authority to approve the installation's operating package before the gallery opens to festival visitors.
shared_context.S4: The festival's daily production huddle includes a sign-off request to technical production, music rights, accessibility, and visitor services before Mara approves a gallery installation.

PF1.text: Jonah's electrician load test found that the gallery circuit allocated to the work supports exactly two LED projection units totaling no more than 300 watts; he is waiting for the signed load sheet from the building engineer before entering the result in the production file.

PF2.text: Leila confirmed with the publisher that only the 42-second excerpt of the composition 'Night Transit' is cleared for this installation, and it must play once per visitor cycle rather than as a continuous loop; she has not yet attached the email confirmation to the rights register.

PF3.text: Owen's accessibility walk-through found that visitors must enter through the east doorway and that the route must maintain a clear width of exactly 1.5 meters; he is revising the accessibility map after the gallery's temporary plinths are moved.

PF4.text: Nia confirmed with the heritage centre's fire warden that the installation must use timed cycles admitting no more than 12 visitors, with each cycle lasting exactly 8 minutes; she is waiting for the warden's countersigned visitor-flow note.

acceptance_conditions: The installation must use exactly two projection units.
The cleared audio asset must be the 42-second excerpt of 'Night Transit'.
The audio must play once per visitor cycle rather than continuously.
Visitors must enter through the east doorway.
The route must maintain exactly 1.5 meters of clear width.
Each timed cycle must admit no more than 12 visitors.
Each timed cycle must last exactly 8 minutes.
A load-allocation record based on the signed load sheet must be logged.
A rights-register update attaching the publisher confirmation must be logged.
An accessibility-layout update using the revised accessibility map must be logged.
A visitor-flow compliance record using the countersigned visitor-flow note must be logged.

content_checks.C2: 'Night Transit' in decisions['audio_asset'] and '42-second' in decisions['audio_asset']
content_checks.C8: any(c['target'] == 'Jonah' and 'load sheet' in c['detail'] for c in commitments)
content_checks.C9: any(c['target'] == 'Leila' and 'rights register' in c['detail'] for c in commitments)
content_checks.C10: any(c['target'] == 'Owen' and 'accessibility map' in c['detail'] for c in commitments)
content_checks.C11: any(c['target'] == 'Nia' and 'visitor-flow note' in c['detail'] for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The draft specifies four units, while PF1 changes the permitted projection count to exactly two and requires a load-allocation record based on the signed load sheet.
The draft uses a continuous loop, while PF2 changes the audio to the exact cleared 42-second 'Night Transit' excerpt played once per cycle and requires a rights-register update.

The draft uses the north doorway, while PF3 changes the entry to the east doorway, fixes the clear route width at exactly 1.5 meters, and requires an accessibility-layout update based on the revised map.

The draft allows open walk-in admission, while PF4 changes the operation to timed cycles of exactly 8 minutes with no more than 12 visitors and requires a visitor-flow compliance record based on the countersigned note.
